gallery.filename: Franciscan Church and Graveyard at Vasai Fort.jpg
gallery.title: File:Franciscan Church and Graveyard at Vasai Fort.jpg
gallery.source: Franciscan Church and Graveyard at Vasai Fort
gallery.description:
🕍 History & Architectural
The Franciscan Church of Saint Anthony was built in 1557 in memory of Saint Anthony of Lisbon, under Portuguese rule inside Vasai Fort.
Its most striking feature is the gravel-strewn floor lined with around 250 tombstones, belonging to Portuguese nobles and clergy. The floor and cloisters reflect both spiritual function and funeral memory.
⚰️ Graveyard
The church floor itself served as a burial site, featuring carved Portuguese epitaphs.
There’s also a Franciscan monastery adjacent now in ruins once serving as the monks cloister and cemetery. Only fragments remain today.

As you walk through the nave of the Franciscan Church, the inscriptions and carved coats of arms on tombstones offer a powerful window into the Portuguese elite’s presence in Vasai.
